* Read a single path component from Wasm memory.
   *
   * Under the handle-only kernel contract this is never a path: the kernel
   * resolves mount routing, `..`, and symlink chains itself and hands this
   * host exactly one component, relative to a directory handle this host
   * previously issued. `"."` names the directory itself, which is how a mount
   * root is addressed. The only exception is a symlink *target*, which is
   * opaque data stored verbatim and never resolved here.
   */
  #readComponentFromMemory(ptr: KernelPointer, len: number): string {
    return new TextDecoder().decode(this.#readKernelBytes(ptr, len));
  }

conclusion: FS-022: guest kernel passes raw component bytes, but host Kernel.#readComponentFromMemory uses default nonfatal TextDecoder and VirtualPlatformIO/backend interfaces take string components. Invalid UTF8 can be reinterpreted as replacement-character names on host-backed routes. Native raw path copying is not end-to-end byte identity; kernel tmpfs uses byte-name maps and is a separate route. This is a host/interface implementation gap, not proof all kernel paths or a browser engine cannot support bytes.
scope: Read-only source excerpts and identity; no executed path probe or native/runtime evidence
